questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer:
The choice of Barcelona was based on the following:
- The city: Barcelona is a great combination of being a big city with great culture along with being a beach city with possibilities to enjoy the coast. 
- The language: One of the main languages in Barcelona together with Catalan is spanish. I lived in South America when I was a child, so the choice of Barcelona was also based on the possibility to improving my spanish language attributes.
- The university: Universitat de Barcelona has received good reviews and offered a bunch of interesting courses.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, the possibility of improving my spanish language attributes, the courses offered at UB and the facilities Barcelona comes with.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Such a giving experience. I can recommend this to everyone.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It could have been better. The university site where frustrating and the employees that we contacted from UB where in doubt when the semester was going to start until 2 weeks before. This could have been more precise in order for us to plan our stay better regarding apartment, travel etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were signed up/registered at the office on our first day of school. This was very effective and Eva was super nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Barcelona is a popular city, hence it was a bit difficult to find a place to live that was inside our budget.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It would have been nice if the institution provided some information on which sites to look at.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't hear anything about cousin available for students. Would have been nice.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration of courses was perfect.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We visited the host institution office when we arrived and got registered at the university. With the pre-approval of courses from KU it was easy for the host insitution to sign us up to the courses, that we have applied for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was a whole office with employees from our faculty ready to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. I got applied for the courses that I originally wanted and planned to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instructions sent to you before the arrival and visit the host institution office for your faculty, they are super helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The way of examining the students with continuous assessment was interesting to try as the examination form in Denmark is only based on one exam. Also, I liked to try the quarter structure.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses was a bit disappointing as some of the courses touched upon topics that was reviewed in courses on the bachelor.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: This was rather different. We got to do referee reports, research proposals and a lot of oral presentations. This differs from the form of teaching in Denmark which was interesting to try.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I took the following courses during my exchange:
- Microeconometrics (2,5 ECTS)
- Macroeconometrics (2,5 ECTS)
- International Trade (5 ECTS)
- Economic Geography (5 ECTS)
- Empirical Approach to Economic Growth (5 ECTS)
- Economic Growth I (5 ECTS)
- Welfare Economics: Education and social policies (5 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic growth was really interesting. I found international trade and welfare economics interesting as well. The other courses was also interesting but some of the parts was already covered in other courses that I have completed on my bachelors degree in Denmark.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Unexpected costs such as transportations costs (to/from the airport), culture attractions. Also the apartment  ended up being really expensive to live in.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, the cost of food and groceries were cheaper in Barcelona relative to Denmark. On the other hand, it was expensive to explore the culture and visit attractions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was super good as well.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports at UB sports. I applied for tennis lessons twice a week. This was very good and not too expensive.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Apply for some sports that you find interesting. I met some good friends from sports.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Do some weekend trips. From Barcelona, we went to costa brava (sunny-vacation), cal barbut (hiking trip), mont rebei (hiking trip) and Girona (old city).

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was rather easy. The society in Barcelona is quite international so the locals speak both spanish/catalan and often also English.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in debates in class, in the breaks etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The students at UB were from all over the world. The challenging part was the communication. The majority speaks English, but the accents are really different. This resulted in lack of understanding of some of the teachers and also other students and hence participation in debates some times.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity of people from all over the world. I found it so interesting to speak with people from middel america, Polen, russia, france and Finland at the same time and discuss society structures, politics and economics.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy every single day and be the best version of yourself.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time with applying for financial support, findings apartments etc.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It is difficult to pick. I enjoyed every moment from trips to everyday life and everything in between.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To get to know everything at a time both new people/social circle, courses and the whole city you live in.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
